progress.title: Exercise progress
progress.weeklyVolumeDescription: Balance of load between large and small muscle groups — check small groups aren't neglected.

charts.workingWeightDescription: The weight used for this exercise in that workout — fixed for the whole exercise, doesn't change between sets. The larger outlined point is a personal weight record.
charts.workingWeightEmpty: This exercise is done without weight
charts.maxRepsDescription: The highest rep count among all sets in that workout (not the sum, not the average). The larger outlined point is a personal reps record.
charts.oneRepMaxDescription: One-rep max — how much you could theoretically lift for 1 rep, via the Epley formula: weight × (1 + reps / 30). Combines weight and reps into a single strength metric, so it keeps rising even when weight drops for higher reps. A rough estimate — the formula gets unreliable past 15+ reps.
charts.oneRepMaxEmpty: This exercise is done without weight
charts.volumeDescriptionWeighted: Total work for the session: weight × sum of reps across all sets. Grows even when weight and max reps stay flat — from doing more sets.
charts.volumeDescriptionBodyweight: For bodyweight exercises — just the sum of reps across all sets in the session.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: MyGym is a personal workout journal. This page explains what data it keeps about you and why. In short: only what is needed to run your training log, nothing is sold or shared.

data.title: What we store
data.body:
• Your email address.
• Your password as a one-way hash (argon2) if you signed up with a password - the password itself is never stored.
• Your Google account ID if you sign in with Google.
• What you enter in the app: exercises, workouts, sets, programs and your training schedule.
• Technical session records (hashes of login tokens) so you stay signed in and can be signed out.
• Server logs with IP addresses and request times, kept for security and troubleshooting.

google.title: Sign in with Google
google.body: If you choose "Continue with Google", MyGym asks Google only for your account ID and email address (the openid and email scopes). It does not get your name, photo, contacts, Gmail, Drive or any other Google data, and it cannot act on your Google account.

use.title: How the data is used
use.body: Only to run the app for you: sign you in, show your workout history and progress charts, and suggest when to add weight or reps. There are no ads, no analytics or tracking services and no profiling.

storage.title: Where it is kept
storage.body: On the MyGym server in a PostgreSQL database, over HTTPS. Your browser keeps a sign-in cookie (httpOnly, up to 30 days so you stay signed in) and remembers your interface language in local storage - no advertising or tracking cookies.

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.body: Your data is not sold, rented or shared with third parties. Other MyGym users cannot see it.

deletion.title: Deleting your data
deletion.body: You can delete individual exercises, workouts and programs in the app at any time. To delete your whole account and all its data, email {{email}} from the address you use in MyGym - it will be removed within 30 days. Server backups may still hold the data until they are rotated out.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions about this policy or your data: {{email}}

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.intro: Connect MyGym to Claude or ChatGPT and the assistant will see your workouts, programs and progress, log sets for you and suggest the plan for the day.
integrations.mcpUrlHint: You will need it at the "paste the URL" step in any app.
integrations.howToHint: Pick the app - it takes 2–3 minutes.

claude.title: Claude
claude.badge: Sign in with MyGym · no token

2.title: Add a custom connector
2.body: Click Add custom connector, name it MyGym and paste the MCP server URL above into the URL field. Click Add.

3.title: Sign in to MyGym
3.body: Click Connect - the MyGym sign-in page opens. Approve access and Claude shows up below in "Connected apps".

4.title: Turn it on in a chat
4.body: In a new chat click + → Connectors and turn MyGym on. Try: "What is on my plan today?"

everywhere.title: Works everywhere
everywhere.body: Add the connector once on claude.ai - it shows up in the Claude desktop and mobile apps too.

team.title: Team or Enterprise?
team.body: The workspace owner has to add the connector in Organization settings → Connectors first.

1.title: Turn on Developer mode
1.body: On chatgpt.com: Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced → turn on Developer mode.

2.title: Create a connector
2.body: Go back to Apps & Connectors and click Create. Name - MyGym, description - "My workouts, programs and progress", URL - the MCP server URL above, authentication - OAuth.

3.title: Sign in to MyGym
3.body: Confirm that you trust the app, click Create and sign in to your MyGym account on the page that opens.

4.title: Pick MyGym in a chat
4.body: In a new chat click + and choose MyGym. It works best when you name it: "Using MyGym, show my latest workouts".

plan.title: Your plan matters
plan.body: Developer mode is not available on every ChatGPT plan, and on some it is read-only. If there is no Create button, check your plan.

browser.title: Start in the browser
browser.body: Add the connector on chatgpt.com; the mobile and desktop apps pick it up after a restart.

1.title: Create a token
1.body: In "Access tokens" below, give the token a name (where you will use it) and copy it - it is shown in full only once.

2.title: Add the server in a terminal

3.title: Check it
3.body: Run claude and type /mcp - MyGym should be connected.

secret.title: A token is like a password
secret.body: Never publish it in repositories. Use a separate token for each client - then you can revoke one without touching the rest.
